findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has misleading logic that always returns false regardless of feature flag
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` contains a negation (`!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`) and an if-branch, but both the if-branch and the fallthrough return `false`. This means the feature flag check is entirely inert—the function always returns false. While this is the intended security behavior (always disable SQL expressions), the code reads as if it has a logic bug. A future maintainer might 'fix' what appears to be an inverted condition or dead code, accidentally re-enabling the vulnerable path. A clearer implementation would be `return false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, making the intent unmistakable and reducing the risk of accidental re-enablement.

findings.title: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is misleading for a deliberately disabled feature
findings.body: The error returned when a user attempts a SQL expression query says 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', but the feature was implemented and is now intentionally disabled due to a critical security vulnerability (CVE-2024-9264). Users or developers debugging this may be confused into thinking the feature was never built. A message like 'sqlExpressions is disabled' or 'sqlExpressions is not available' would be more accurate and less likely to lead someone to try to 'implement' it again.

findings.title: No tests verify that SQL expressions are blocked
findings.body: This PR disables a feature that had a critical RCE/LFI vulnerability (CVE-2024-9264), but no test is added to assert that `ReadQuery` returns an error for `QueryTypeSQL`. Without a test, a future refactor could silently remove the guard or change the code path, re-exposing the vulnerability. A unit test calling `ReadQuery` with a SQL-type query and asserting the error would provide a regression safety net for this security fix.

findings.title: Stub DB lacks documentation explaining it is a security mitigation
findings.body: The new `DB` struct and `NewInMemoryDB` function replace the real DuckDB-backed implementation as a security fix, but there is no comment explaining why all methods return 'not implemented'. Without context, a developer might think this is incomplete work and attempt to re-implement the DuckDB integration, potentially reintroducing the vulnerability. A package-level or function-level comment referencing the CVE and the intentional disabling would prevent this.
